entertainment.title: Druski Embodies Elizabeth Holmes in ‘You Can See Everything’ Spoof on ‘SNL’
entertainment.summary: The comedian gave his own take on Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's documentary, instead entitled 'Dru Can See Everything.'
entertainment.body:
Logo text You really can see just about everything on Saturday Night Live — even Druski dressed up as Elizabeth Holmes .

During the comedian’s SNL debut , the show spoofed on the success of Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything with a fresh take on its origins.

As the skit went, before Fielder and Oppenheim signed on to direct the project, Druski was originally attached to the doc. Jane Wickline appeared in the sketch as Elizabeth Holmes while Ben Marshall portrayed Holmes’ husband, Billy Evans. Related Stories TV James Talarico Crashes 'SNL' Cold Open, Apologizes for Texting Us So Much TV Emma Stone Joins Druski During His 'SNL' Hosting Debut

“We’re so glad you’re here,” Wickline’s Holmes said, as Marshall’s Evans added, “It’s really important to us that people find out who Liz really is, you know.”

“I just want people to see me as an ordinary person. Can you do that, Druski?” the faux Holmes asked. Druski replied, “Based on what I’ve seen so far, I’m gonna go ahead and say no. Y’all got some of the weirdest, freakiest vibes I have ever seen.”

SNL poked fun at the close-up shots featured in You Can See Everything , with Druski and Wickline recreating the infamous moment from the doc where Fielder and Holmes converse about whether the latter was trying to deceive the filmmaker.

And while Fielder and Oppenheim’s doc “was a three-hour cinematic epic,” the show joked that “Druski’s tape was released on Instagram Reels in a 1,000 part series titled ‘Crazy White Lady Skit.'”

Referencing the comedian’s own popular mock audition show Coulda Been Love , he even had Marshall’s Evans perform a song of his own. “My name is Billy and I make eight figures, can’t believe I’m here with all my –” he said before being cut off.

entertainment.title: James Talarico Crashes ‘SNL’ Cold Open, Apologizes for Texting Us So Much
entertainment.summary: The Texas senator-elect also took a shot at the show's reliance on James Austin Johnson's Donald Trump impression in his surprise appearance in front of the comic.
entertainment.body:
Logo text James Austin Johnson was born for this moment — Donald Trump spinning as he is roundly defeated by Democrats — and he rose to meet in Saturday Night Live ’s cold open.

But it was a Democratic politician who stole the show from Trump’s 2026 defeatism tour, as Texas senator-elect James Talarico made a surprise appearance as himself at the end of the sketch.

“I’m James Talarico, the guy who’s been texting you every day asking for five dollars,” the popular Texas politician said as he came out on stage to gasps and cheers from the audience, with Trump mumbly meta-jibing behind him, “In this economy, who can blame you?” Related Stories TV Emma Stone Joins Druski During His 'SNL' Hosting Debut TV After 2026 Midterms, Bill Maher Asks Trump, "Donnie, Are You OK?"

Talarico a moment later invoked the iconic “Live from New York” with Johnson. Talarico drubbed his Republican opponent Ken Paxton by 12 points in the most expensive race in the history of the United States Senate, in part on the back of the grassroots fundraising campaign he was self-mocking on SNL . The result turned a Texas Senate seat blue for the first time in over 30 years.

Before Talarico showed up in Studio 8H, Johnson had been reveling in his presidential character’s anti-moment.

“I didn’t even say it was rigged,” Trump said of the election tallies. “I accepted the results, which is even scarier in a way. It’s like, ‘What the hell is he planning?'” He then said he only cared about his newly redesigned White House ballroom, before allowing under his breath, “Oh my God, I hate my life.”

Talarico’s cold-open surprise cameo echoed moments like Kamala Harris’ 2024 turn-up, in which she played opposite her celebrity impersonator Maya Rudolph ahead of the election, while Hillary Clinton and Sarah Palin also made unexpected appearances as White House candidates more than a decade ago. A senator or senator-elect, however, is rarer, and the moment both reflected and reinforced the emergent media celebrity of the new class of Congressional Democrats, many of them in their 30s or early 40s.

“The next few years are going to be horrible,” he said, pausing a comic beat. “It’s not that they’re Democrats; it’s that they’re Millennials.” He then lamented the return of generational staples like “adorkable” and the show New Girl .

entertainment.title: Emma Stone Joins Druski During His ‘SNL’ Hosting Debut
entertainment.summary: The Oscar winner and comedian will co-star in the Universal Pictures rom-com The Catch, which hits theaters on May 21, 2027.
entertainment.body:
Logo text Druski made his Saturday Night Live debut with an assist from his upcoming co-star Emma Stone .

He kicked off his first-ever monologue by acknowledging that his appearance marked the first time an online content creator hosted the show.

“It is a dream to be hosting Saturday Night Live . Apparently, people are saying I’m the first internet content creator, social media influencer, only make you laugh on your phone, TikTok and YouTube and Instagram star to host this show,” he said. “Woo. People say a lot of things about me, honestly.” Related Stories TV 'SNL' Writer Jimmy Fowlie Pays Tribute to Sister Christina Downer After Police Arrest Two for Her Murder TV Druski Signs Deal With Netflix, Sets Church Comedy 'Collect & Praise'

“Some people say I look like a lesbian. I don’t know how true that is,” Druski joked. “Some people say I’m on Ozempic. Could be lies, could be truth to that.”

Druski, whose real name is Drew Desbordes, admitted that SNL would not be “holding me back from saying anything.” He said there were only a few rules to follow: No cussing and no “whiteface,” which he both joked he couldn’t promise to. (More on that later.)

“But honestly, this is a huge moment for me growing up as a fat kid from the suburbs. Why y’all laughing? My teachers never believed in me, so I just wanna say… Yeah, I’m just lying. I just wanted to say that because rappers be saying that type of stuff,” he joked, before thanking his family, who was in the audience, for supporting his dreams.

“I’m so grateful. When I first started my career, I let them, let me turn my dreams into a full-blown movie convention. Every day I think about how could I possibly repay y’all,” he began, as one of his family members offered, “Some money!”

The comedian recounted the growth his career has seen in recent years, noting, “I am living proof you can bet on yourself and make your dreams come true.” He added, “I just finished filming my first ever movie with Emma Stone, and she is here right now!” The Oscar winner then entered the stage, and the two recounted their time working on The Catch together.

entertainment.title: U2 Weigh In on Ed Sheeran and Macklemore Tour Controversy
entertainment.summary: The Edge and Larry Mullen Jr. defended the rapper’s right to speak out, while the Edge said Sheeran “should not be vilified”.
entertainment.body:
U2 have weighed in on Macklemore ’s removal from Ed Sheeran ’s U.S. tour, backing the rapper’s right to speak out while cautioning against blaming Sheeran.

“We totally support Macklemore ’s right as an artist to say what he wanted to say,” the Edge said in an interview with BBC News. “I don’t think Ed should be vilified,” he added, acknowledging the difficult position Sheeran had been in. The guitarist also praised the artists who left Sheeran’s tour in solidarity, framing the dispute as a matter of free expression. Related Deep Purple's Ian Gillan Shares Encouraging News After Undergoing Surgery Richard Lloyd, Television Guitarist, Dies at 75 Benson Boone Brings Young Fan Battling Cancer Onstage at Brisbane Concert Explore Ed Sheeran Macklemore U2 See latest videos, charts and news

Drummer Larry Mullen Jr. went further. “Artists can choose whether they want to be politically active or not. It’s a human right,” he said. “But we as a band will fight for the right to speak your mind as long as it doesn’t incite violence. And even if we disagree with it or don’t like it, nobody has a right – no billionaire, no promoter, no owner has the right to censor anybody. They will definitely not be censoring us ever.”

Macklemore was dropped from the North American leg of Sheeran’s Loop Tour in September after two opening sets at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, where he said “Free Palestine,” spoke about Gaza and the West Bank, and performed his protest song “Hind’s Hall.” Promoter Messina Touring Group said venues on the remaining dates would not allow the shows to go ahead with him on the bill.

New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft confirmed he barred the rapper from Gillette Stadium, citing his comments and what Kraft called “a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery.”

Sheeran said the decision belonged to the promoter. Several acts left the tour in response, including Finneas, Lukas Graham and Irish folk band Beoga, which had been performing with Sheeran each night. Sheeran later opened a show in Philadelphia by apologizing for “mistakes” in his handling of the situation.

Macklemore has since played three sold-out Free Palestine benefit concerts in Dublin, Paris and London, with guests including Hozier, Kneecap and Beoga, raising money for organizations supporting Palestinians.

U2 release Carnaval De Luz , their 16th studio album and first full-length of new material in nine years, on Nov. 13. The album closes with “Torn,” a duet with the late Dolly Parton that the band says was her last recorded vocal performance.

entertainment.title: Simple Plan Are Meeting a Whole New Generation of Fans, 25 Years In
entertainment.summary: Drummer Chuck Comeau talks TikTok, Good Things Festival, and why a farewell tour is “not in the cards”
entertainment.body:
Simple Plan have been playing the same songs for 25 years. Lately, they’re playing them to a lot of people hearing them live for the first time.

“Every night we ask people, ‘Hey, how many people are here for the first time?’” drummer Chuck Comeau tells Billboard. “Sometimes it’s like 85% have never seen the band.”

The Montreal pop-punk band is drawing fans who weren’t born when “I’m Just a Kid” arrived in 2002, alongside the original listeners who are now bringing their own kids to shows. Some of the younger crowd have even started calling Simple Plan “classic rock.” Related Deep Purple's Ian Gillan Shares Encouraging News After Undergoing Surgery Richard Lloyd, Television Guitarist, Dies at 75 Benson Boone Brings Young Fan Battling Cancer Onstage at Brisbane Concert Explore Simple Plan See latest videos, charts and news

“And you’re like, ‘What are you talking about?’” Comeau says.

“There’s nothing cooler than what’s happening to our band right now,” he adds.

Much of that can be traced to “I’m Just a Kid” going viral on TikTok , where it soundtracked a challenge encouraging users to recreate their childhood photos. Comeau calls the trend a “gigantic gift,” but says meeting fans online has always come naturally to the band, which was filming backstage antics and sharing them through its website and DVDs long before TikTok existed.

The renewed attention builds on a strong early run. The band’s 2004 album Still Not Getting Any… debuted at No. 3 on the Billboard 200, while “Perfect” and “Welcome to My Life” reached Nos. 24 and 40, respectively, on the Billboard Hot 100.

Next up is a return to Australia for Good Things Festival, where Simple Plan join a bill led by Limp Bizkit and featuring Spiritbox , the All-American Rejects , Bad Religion and MxPx. entertainment.title: 5 Best Sitcom Grandmas Of All Time, Ranked
entertainment.summary: Some sitcom grandmas offer warmth and wisdom, while others bring chaos and laughs. These five memorable characters prove there's no one way to be a grandma
entertainment.body:
NBC Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover A staple archetype in many beloved family sitcoms is the grandmother, and while they are usually not the protagonists, they frequently steal the show. Why wouldn't they? Our love and adoration for our grandmas make us gravitate toward that character, and the mere existence of these characters usually creates an immediate emotional connection.

While some of the most popular grandmas might fit the doting and wise category, such as Anna Huxtable in "The Cosby Show," the grandma archetype certainly is not limited to just sage advice and unconditional love. There's the bitter grandma who's a walking fuse or the one who always has a quip ready, just to name a few. The variety of different types of grandmas, and the actresses who give such memorable performances in this list, are certainly worth celebrating too.

FOX A prime example of a family member who exudes malice and hatred for her kin, Ida Welker subverts the kind grandma trope by going to the opposite extreme in "Malcolm in the Middle." Introduced in Season 2, Episode 15, "The Grandparents," the character was portrayed by Cloris Leachman, who won two Primetime Emmy Awards for Outstanding Guest Actress in a Comedy Series for the role.

What makes Ida Welker one of the best sitcom grandmas is the sheer chaos she brings every time she comes into the house. She showed no affection, gave no advice, and provided no comfort. She referred to Francis's wife, Piama, as a maid, piled on household stress onto the pregnant Lois, and was abusive to Lois' son, Francis. While the show gave her a moment of heroism in "Ida Loses a Leg," when she saves Dewey from an oncoming truck, this didn't undo her sins.

Fortunately, for fans who could not stand the character, Ida Welker only appeared in 11 episodes. While it may seem paradoxical to consider her one of the best sitcom grandmas after listing all her negative traits, it is precisely her personality that makes her such an uncomfortable force of nature to watch.

ABC "Black-ish" explores family in the context of African American culture and all its nuances, and Jenifer Lewis' Ruby Johnson is a critical part of that. Making her first appearance in Season 1, Episode 8, "Oedipal Triangle," she went from a guest character to a regular in Season 3. The mother of Andre Johnson (Anthony Anderson), wife of Pops (Laurence Fishburne), and mother-in-law to Rainbow Johnson (Tracee Ellis Ross), her story concluded in the series finale, "Homegoing," when she and Pops went on a cross-country adventure.

HBO Max/YouTube Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover For years, HBO has been one of the biggest names in creating unique, original television. So, it makes perfect sense that its streaming platform, HBO Max, has so thoroughly embraced animation and all the storytelling it has to offer.

The streaming platform has added some of the best and most creative animated TV shows ever made to its library while also producing original series of its own. Whether it's family-friendly shows that kids and adults can enjoy or dark, depressing, and hyper-violent adult animation, HBO Max is streaming cartoons that will have viewers glued to their seats.

It's hard to think of a better streaming platform for animated content to live. The medium allows creators to bring imaginative worlds to life that would be difficult, if not prohibitively expensive, to recreate in live action. So, for the network that brought the world big worlds in shows like "Game of Thrones," "The Last of Us," "Dune: Prophecy," and even "Lanterns," animation is a pretty logical place for the likes of some of the below animated shows.

Whether you're looking to laugh, think, or cry, these shows that are currently streaming on HBO Max are sure to get you where you're going.

HBO Max It's often a no-brainer to take a popular comic book and bring it to life through animation, which is exactly what happened with creator Todd McFarlane's "Spawn."

Based on the character from Image Comics, the show premiered on HBO in 1997 as a rare foray into adult animation. At a time when the majority of cartoons were thought to be for children, McFarlane and HBO recognized its potential to tell grown-up stories and used the immensely dark character of Spawn to do so. And boy, is the animated "Spawn" a dark show.

When it initially came out in 1997, it was overshadowed by the live-action movie that released the same year. Over time, it became a favorite among fans who appreciated its writing, high-quality animation, and willingness to tell dramatic, violent, and sexually explicit stories through cartoons. The show is a faithful adaptation of the Image Comics character and, despite its three-season run ending in 1999, holds up as an animated classic to this day.

entertainment.title: Patrick Stewart Wrote And Performed His Own Humor-Fueled Eulogy 11 Years Ago
entertainment.summary: The late Patrick Stewart once took a comedy festival stage and delivered one of the filthiest, most unexpected performances of his entire career.
entertainment.body:
Rich Fury/Getty Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover It is a given in life that no one will ever hear their own eulogy, unless, like Sir Patrick Stewart, they write their own while they're living. Though Stewart was best known for his acting career on stage and on screen, in 2015, the British star gave comedy a try when he hosted a gala at the Just for Laughs festival in Montreal. After a string of comedians performed, Stewart closed the night contemplating the end of his life and delivering a hilarious, scandalous eulogy.

Stewart, who was 75 at the time, committed to the bit, even referring to himself in the third person. Early in the brief eulogy, Stewart says, "He was also a husband and a father and a friend. But most of all, he was an objectophile who achieved sexual congress with literally thousands of inanimate objects." The "Star Trek: The Next Generation" actor carried on that joke throughout the eulogy, rattling off a few objects he had inappropriate relations with. This included the very seats in the venue, which Stewart joked he had "rubbed his unwashed genitals" on.

Fans were surprised by these dirty jokes since Stewart normally plays respectable or regal characters in film and TV such as Jean-Luc Picard or Charles Xavier. Eleven years after this event, Stewart died in his home after being diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia. In October 2026, his loved ones, fans, and former costars honored the "Star Trek" actor in more positive and appropriate ways.

Starz/YouTube Patrick Stewart fans would normally not class the "X-Men" star as a comedy actor, but Stewart has a long history of comedic roles. On the big screen, Stewart starred in Mel Brooks' spoof "Robin Hood: Men in Tights" and narrated "Ted" and "Ted 2." The "Star Trek" actor had an unusual role in the dark comedy series "Bait," as he played a talking pig's head. Stewart was a voice actor in "American Dad" from its first season in 2005 until his death, and lent his voice to "Family Guy," "The Simpsons," and "The Emoji Movie."

Stewart famously played himself on Ricky Gervais' Hollywood satirical show "Extras," where he pitches a ludicrous movie about women's clothes falling off in front of him. But the "Star Trek" star had a main role in a sitcom only once in his career — in a show that was produced by Seth MacFarlane, who created "Ted," "Family Guy," and "American Dad." In "Blunt Talk," Stewart played a British newscaster who moves to America to conquer the news world there, but his dream is thwarted by his own incompetence as well as his colleagues' ineptitude.

entertainment.title: Blue Bloods' Stars Were Allowed To Eat Their Family Dinner If They Followed One Rule
entertainment.summary: Family dinners were a crucial part of life for the Regan family of "Blue Bloods." Actors could eat from the abundant prop food, as long as one rule was abided.
entertainment.body:
Pluto TV/CBS Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover The Reagan family dinners on "Blue Bloods" are the heart of the series, giving the characters a chance to come together after a long, hard week in law enforcement. These scenes were important for the cast too, according to star Donnie Wahlberg. "It's an incredible blessing to have that dinner scene as a check-in every week, much like the Reagans do, fictionally," he shared in an interview with Emmy Magazine, as reported by People .

But the dinner scenes were far more laborious to film than they might seem, and the cast followed certain rules to make the shoots as seamless as possible. In an interview with the Virginian-Pilot , "Blue Bloods" prop master Jim Lillis shared some behind-the-scenes secrets from the filming of these dinner scenes. He answered an age-old question about on-screen meals: do the actors actually eat their food?

According to Lillis, he had one rule regarding food consumption. Actors were allowed to munch on the food if they so pleased, but they were prohibited from delivering their lines with their mouths full.

Pluto TV/CBS According to "Blue Bloods" patriarch, Tom Selleck , the family dinners took six to eight hours to film, which is a rather long time to be eating — or pretending to eat — a meal. Selleck revealed some of the tricks of the trade at a PaleyFest panel, as reported by Entertainment Weekly . "Bridget [Moynahan] is a food masher. She keeps her hand real active and combines her potatoes and everything. I butter rolls," he shared.

Vanessa Ray, who played Eddie Lanko, was initially too enthusiastic at her first dinner scenes, before realizing her mistake. "I kept eating and I realized, 'Oh, you can't eat 17 rolls,'" she explained.

entertainment.title: Jason Priestley reveals what could have saved Shannen Doherty from getting fired from ‘Beverly Hills, 90210’
entertainment.summary: Doherty, who played Priestley's on-screen twin sister, exited the series at the end of its fourth season.
entertainment.body:
Jason Priestley believes Shannen Doherty being more open about her personal struggles could have changed the outcome of her time on “Beverly Hills, 90210.”

During Thursday’s episode of Pete Ferriero’s “The Slice of Life Show” podcast , Priestley, who played Brandon Walsh on the iconic ’90s teen drama, reflected on Doherty’s “disruptive” on-set behavior that led to her departure.

“There was never an issue between her and I specifically,” he said. “I loved Shannen. I loved working with her. She was a great actress. She was a great scene partner. I only have fond memories of working with her on the show.”

Doherty, who played Brenda Walsh, twin sister of Priestley’s Brandon, exited the series at the end of its fourth season, with the show ultimately going on to run for 10 seasons.

When asked whether he thought letting her go was the “right move,” Priestley, 57, admitted, “That’s a tough question.”

“I feel like, given the information that we had, we made the only choice that we could,” he added. “Had Shannen been more forthcoming about what was happening with her in her life at that point in time, I think we could have made a different choice.”

The “Wild Cards” actor went to explain that Doherty’s departure was “scary” for him and the rest of the cast, describing her as “part of the secret sauce that made the show successful.”

“We were going to lose that. As much as we knew it was going to impact her life and her career, we knew it was going to impact our show as well,” he said. “The decision to let her go was not one that was taken lightly.”

entertainment.title: Alanis Morissette Shares She Identifies as Pansexual
entertainment.summary: The singer-songwriter chatted about it briefly in a podcast appearance the week of releasing her new holiday album.
entertainment.body:
Alanis Morissette identifies as pansexual, she revealed in a podcast appearance earlier this week. The hitmaker — who just dropped her first holiday album, Good Weather for Immaculate Conception , featuring new single “To an Empath at Christmas Time” — visited the Handsome Podcast as the podcast trio’s first in-person guest for an episode that was uploaded on Nov. 3.

“I’m sorry for the men that hurt you, but I’m not sorry for the songs that came from it. Those are pretty amazing,” comedian Fortune Feimster, who co-hosts the show with Tig Notaro and Mae Martin, said at one point toward the end of the episode, adding, “Did it make you want to be a lesbian at any point?”

“I’m pansexual, so yeah,” Morissette shared in reply. “I get everything.”

GLAAD defines someone who identifies as pansexual as “a person who has the capacity to form enduring physical, romantic, and/ or emotional attractions to any person, regardless of gender identity.” The term is different than the term bisexual, which means that a person is attracted to people of more than one gender (whereas pansexual means gender is not a determining factor in attraction).

Notaro then asked, “Wait, you’re not really pansexual, are you?” to which Morissette confirmed, “I am.”

Joking that they should’ve launched the episode with this tidbit, Notaro said, “How did I not know this?”

“You know, I like to leave it for the epilogue,” quipped Morissette. “I like to confuse people on the way out. Is it confusing?”

Morissette, who’s got three Billboard 200 No. 1 albums under her belt and whose top hit “Ironic” soared to No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1996, is married to husband Mario Treadway, aka the artist Souleye. The couple wed in 2010 and are parents to three children.

entertainment.summary: The former *NSYNC singer and the pop star dated from 1999 to 2002.
entertainment.body:
Justin Timberlake has finally revealed that his hit 2006 song, “What Goes Around… Comes Around,” was not written about ex-girlfriend Britney Spears.

Since its debut, many have believed that the song was about Spears, as it came out around the time the pop star was divorcing Kevin Federline. However, that’s just not the case, according to Timberlake.

“Maybe I should dispel a rumor at this point, which has gone around forever, which is like, it’s not a personal story from mine,” Timberlake said during a recent appearance on Complex’s “Re-Rank” YouTube series.

“It’s actually a personal story from a friend’s that I asked permission [to use],” he said of the track, which was a single off his 2006 album, “FutureSex/LoveSounds.”

Timberlake, 45, explained that the song was informed by a friend’s breakup.

“He was just going through it and he was telling me what had happened, and I said, ‘Do you mind if I write about this?’ And I quote, my friend said, ‘Yeah, torch that bitch. What goes around comes around.’ And I was like, ‘I have to go. Thank you,’” Timberlake recalled.

The “Mirrors” singer said that he wrote the song in “damn near 20 minutes.”

Paired with the 10-minute long music video, he said it “hit on all cylinders” for him. In the YouTube show, Timberlake ranked the song as number “one or two” in his discography.

entertainment.title: Mariska Hargitay Starred In A Forgotten HBO Series From Twin Peaks Creator David Lynch
entertainment.summary: Before becoming Olivia Benson, Mariska Hargitay appeared in an obscure HBO project with ties to one of television's most unconventional creative minds.
entertainment.body:
DFree/Shutterstock Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Before Mariska Hargitay landed her star role on "Law & Order: Special Victims Unit," she starred in a little-known project of David Lynch's. The project was the three-part HBO miniseries "Hotel Room." Each episode focuses on the same New York City hotel room in a different time period: the first takes place in 1969, the second in 1992, and the third in 1936. Hargitay plays a woman named Diane in the second episode; she's not the main focus, but she is a constant presence in the first half as she hangs out in the titular hotel room with her friends Sasha (Debora Kara Unger) and Tina (Chelsea Field).

Hargitay's episode is a charming, dialogue-driven story with a lot of energetic jazz music playing in the background. Hargitay's character spends much of her screen time talking about dating with her friends; the episode was criticized at the time for being a little too relaxed and slow-paced, but honestly, it's just a fun time watching these women hang out and chat. The three women give off a similar vibe to the gossipy female trio in Season 3 of "The White Lotus," where they get along well, but the viewer can sense tension brewing before Sasha's boyfriend shows up and she smashes him over the head with a statue.

HBO/YouTube Mariska Hargitay is the daughter of Jayne Mansfield, a major Hollywood star and sex symbol in the '50s and '60s. Despite her mother's success, Hargitay told the Vancouver Sun in 1986 that as a kid she hadn't been interested in acting. "Acting had nothing to do with my life," she said. "Every week I changed my idea of what I wanted to be."

It wasn't until the mid-'80s, when a casting director for the upcoming police drama "Downtown" was looking for someone with what Hargitay described as "Amy Madigan" vibes and invited her to an audition, that she realized on-screen acting might be a good fit. For the next few years, she played a wide range of TV characters, including one in the hit '80s soap opera "Falcon Crest," and in the early '90s she began starring in more dramas. Of course, this eventually led to her iconic role as Olivia Benson, making Hargitay the longest-running actor in a primetime drama.

Although Hargitay has always maintained that she's proud of her mother's career — she told the Vancouver Sun that Mansfield was much more than the "sex bombshell" persona Hollywood gave her — she seemed more interested in establishing herself as a darker, grittier performer early in her career. Hargitay's participation in "Hotel Room" coincided with a major role in the dark HBO film "Blind Spot," in which she proved her ability to handle some truly disturbing material. The film features a controversial rape scene, for instance, which (as she told a Tribune Media Services reporter) she found "really hard, uncomfortable" to film. Apparently drawn to these dramatic, difficult storylines, it makes sense that she couldn't turn down the part in the miniseries by David Lynch, who already made film history with "Eraserhead" and "Blue Velvet."

entertainment.title: Camerimage Founder Marek Zydowicz on AI, Aronofsky and Why “Cinematographers Are Artists, Not Technicians”
entertainment.summary: As Camerimage turns 34, its director explains how the world's leading festival on the art of cinematography continues to embrace new technology while drawing the line on fully AI-generated films.
entertainment.body:
Camerimage , the world’s premier festival devoted to the art of cinematography, turns 34 this year, and it arrives in Torun, Poland, Nov. 7-14, with its founder in both a combative and reflective mood.

Marek Zydowicz, who launched the event in 1993 to champion cinematographers and other below-the-line artists the industry treated as mere technicians, is fielding questions on a thorny set of issues. Among them: the rise of generative AI , which gets its own debates and workshops this year; the squeeze on budgets and theatrical releases; and the decision to honor Darren Aronofsky , an outspoken AI adopter, with the festival’s director award. Related Stories Movies PÖFF Stands With Ukraine: A Look at Films Featured at Tallinn Made Despite, and Because of, the War Oscars 2027: Int'l Films in Focus 'Hold Onto Me,' Cyprus' First Oscar Hopeful, Stars a Newcomer and a 'Dogtooth' Actor in a Very Personal Father-Daughter Drama

Joe Walker, the editor behind Dune and 12 Years a Slave , is also being feted and will chair the Main Competition jury, while Polish cinematographer Janusz Kaminski, whose Disclosure Day is screening in contention, receives THR ’s Visionary award .

Speaking to THR ahead of this year’s fest, Zydowicz said Camerimage will remain open to a “diversity of techniques and technologies” but draws the line at fully AI-generated films.

In a wide-ranging conversation, Zydowicz spoke about the festival’s growing ambitions, the reason why Poland seems to produce so many great cinematographers, and why the human eye will never be replaced.

Why are there so many extraordinary Polish cinematographers? What’s the secret?

A full answer would require going quite far back into the history of Polish cinema, and even further, to the period when Poland was partitioned. For 123 years, paintings and graphic works depicting the most important events in our nation’s history sustained our hopes of regaining independence and stirred our imaginations and dreams. After the second World War, this tradition of depicting the past played an enormously important role in laying the foundations of the Lodz Film School.

Artists working under communist censorship often drew on the same ways of expressing what could not be said openly as their predecessors had in the nineteenth century. Sometimes the dialogue between characters told one story while the images suggested another. This encouraged the development of an extraordinary sensitivity and a search for ways of using composition to smuggle forbidden content and aesthetics into films. Technological limitations and Poland’s isolation from the most progressive developments in Western culture made it necessary to find original solutions of our own.

sports.title: Deion Sanders says Colorado deserves better after falling to 3-6
sports.summary: Colorado lost again on Saturday night, and afterward head coach Deion Sanders said he knows his team isn't good enough.
sports.body:
Saturday’s 20-10 loss to Arizona State dropped Colorado to 3-6 this season, and dropped Sanders to 19-27 in four years as Colorado’s head coach.

“The season doesn’t look good,” Sanders said afterward. “It doesn’t look good. I’m not crazy. I can see clearly. You think I’m happy? I’m not happy with the outcomes. I’m not a loser by any means, and I hate the fact that we’re coming up on the short end of these games.”

Sanders said he feels for Colorado fans and players because he doesn’t think he has done enough to put them in a position to win.

“It’s not a personal hurt for me, I hurt because you guys deserve better and the team deserves better. We should win. We should put our best foot forward. And I’m not seeing that,” Sanders said.

Sanders ran through the stats from the game and then said his team hadn’t played well enough.

“The fan base deserves better. They really do,” Sanders said.

“We’ve just got to do better,” Sanders said. “And that starts with me.”

sports.summary: The Broncos keep finding ways to win games — especially close games.

Denver has won 16 straight games decided by one score or less. Quarterback Bo Nix has been the starter in each of the games.

Via NBC Sports research, the streak ties the 2023-24 Chiefs (with starting quarterback Patrick Mahomes) for the longest streak since 1950.

The Broncos last lost a one-score game in Week 3 of the 2025 season, 23-20 at the Chargers. Since then, the Broncos have won every one-score game in which they have played.

This year, they’re doing it despite being routinely outgained. For the season, they have a yardage differential of minus-658 — third worst in the NFL. And the Broncos have won three games in 2026 despite being outgained by 100 or more yards.

The record for any season is four wins, accomplished by eight different teams. With two more this year, the Broncos will have the record to themselves.

sports.title: Player Personnel Handbook implies that the NFL can delay (or deny) Brandon Aiyuk's reinstatement
sports.summary: The CBA is silent on the issue.
sports.body:
The Brandon Aiyuk case shows that, in the NFL’s view, it definitely is not.

The Collective Bargaining Agreement is silent on the topic of the reserve/left squad list. The relevant language regarding placement (and eventual reinstatement) from the reserve/left squad list appears in the NFL’s Player Personnel Handbook.

In the year when the player is placed on reserve/left squad, he can’t play for his current team or any other team. His season is basically over. The window for reinstatement opens the next year.

Here’s the key language from the Player Personnel Handbook regarding reinstatement: “A player on Reserve/Left Squad must apply to the Commissioner for reinstatement to his club’s Active List. No player on Reserve/Left Squad shall be reinstated in the same season in which he is placed on Reserve. A player applying for reinstatement in a season subsequent to the season in which he is placed on Reserve/Left Squad is prohibited from being reinstated in the last 30 days of the regular season or thereafter during the postseason, and no such player will be reinstated during the period between the trading deadline of a subsequent season and the 30-day deadline unless the club initiates the reinstatement request and the Commissioner approves it.”

While the provision doesn’t say it expressly, the language implies that the Commissioner has apparently unlimited discretion when it comes to approving the application to reinstate the player. In Aiyuk’s case, the Commissioner has dragged his feet since October 27, setting the stage for an apparent effort by the 49ers to leverage Aiyuk’s desire to be reinstated to his willingness to reimburse up to $13 million in previously-paid bonus money.

The NFL Players Association has remained silent throughout the process, and perhaps for good reason. The absence of any provision in the CBA regarding the mechanics of the reserve/left squad list arguably means that the situation falls within the NFL’s “management rights” clause, which allows the various teams “to manage and direct their operations in any manner whatsoever, except as specifically limited by the provisions of this Agreement.”

With no limitations in the CBA as to the operation of the reserve/left squad list (or reinstatement from it), the NFLPA may be without options.

Precedent becomes relevant to the overall analysis. How has the league handled past requests for reinstatement from the reserve/left squad list? If the league has previously not delayed reinstatement (for whatever reason), there’s an argument to be made that it should not be delayed as to Aiyuk.

It’s unclear why the league didn’t fine McCormick. The league never explains the basis for not imposing a financial penalty on a given player.

Regardless, the league was as unbothered by the play as the other Browns players were. And it’s likely that Verse will have something to say about it after Sunday’s game at the Saints.

sports.title: Amherst native Rob Gronkowski enters Patriots Hall of Fame
sports.summary: The former Williamsville North standout and NFL star tight end is being inducted into the Patriots Hall of Fame this weekend.

sports.title: 49ers activate Demarcus Robinson, elevate KhaDarel Hodge
sports.summary: The 49ers will have two of their Week 1 wideouts back in the lineup for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
sports.body:
Demarcus Robinson has been activated from injured reserve and KhaDarel Hodge has been elevated from the practice squad. Wide receiver Christian Kirk went on injured reserve in a corresponding move.

Robinson caught a touchdown in that Week 1 win over the Rams, but has been out since injuring his ankle the next week. Hodge played in the first three games of the season as a practice squad elevation, but was released in October. He returned to the team this week.

Kirk injured his knee in practice this week. He opened the season on injured reserve and made his 2026 debut in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons.

sports.title: NFL fines Roquan Smith $35K for unflagged hits against the Bills, Josh Allen
sports.summary: Bills fans noticed it during the game. Now the NFL has weighed in. A Ravens defender has been fined more than $35,000 for two hits on Bills players.

sports.title: Broncos activate WR Pat Bryant
sports.summary: The Broncos have wide receiver Pat Bryant back for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
sports.body:
Bryant was activated from injured reserve on Saturday afternoon. He missed four games with an ankle injury and was designated for return when he resumed practicing with the team this week.

Bryant had nine catches for 133 yards and a touchdown in four games before his injury.

The Broncos also signed cornerback Sean Fresch off of the practice squad and placed defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike on injured reserve. Uwazurike was ruled out for Sunday with a shoulder injury.

Safety Taylor Rapp and running back Cody Schrader were elevated from the practice squad in other moves.

sports.title: Lions place LB Jack Campbell on injured reserve
sports.summary: The Lions placed linebacker Jack Campbell on injured reserve, the team announced Saturday.
sports.body:
Campbell injured his neck during last week’s victory over the Vikings and remains hospitalized. Campbell released a statement earlier this week saying he has full movement in his lower body and continues to make progress with movement in his upper body.

Trevor Nowaske is expected to start for Campbell alongside Derrick Barnes and Malcolm Rodriguez.

In a corresponding move, the Lions signed cornerback Nick Whiteside from the practice squad. Whiteside has not played in 2026 but played nine games for the Lions last season.

The Lions also announced the elevations of defensive end Anthony Lucas and running back Jabari Small from the practice squad.

sports.title: Saints activate Kelvin Banks, Jordyn Tyson
sports.summary: The Saints offense will be getting a couple of reinforcements for Sunday's game against the Browns.
sports.body:
They announced that they have activated left tackle Kelvin Banks and wide receiver Jordyn Tyson from injured reserve. Banks has been out since suffering an ankle injury in Week 2 and Tyson has yet to play this season due to a hamstring injury. Tyson was a first-round pick this season, so Sunday’s game will be his NFL debut.

As previously reported, the Saints released running back Kendre Miller in a corresponding move. They also released tight end Treyton Welch.

Kicker Charlie Smyth and running back Zamir White have been elevated from the practice squad on a temporary basis.

sports.title: Falcons activate James Pearce, Yasir Abdullah
sports.summary: Falcons linebacker James Pearce is set to make his 2026 debut.
sports.body:
Pearce was suspended for the first eight games of the season as a result of a domestic violence arrest and the team officially moved him to their active roster on Saturday. Pearce had 10.5 sacks as a rookie and he’ll try to add to that total against Joe Burrow and the Bengals in Madrid on Sunday.

The Falcons also activated Yasir Abdullah from injured reserve, so they’ll have a couple of new options on the edge this weekend.

Wide receiver Beaux Collins came off of injured reserve as well and the Falcons signed running back Khalil Herbert off of the practice squad. He’s filled in for the injured Brian Robinson the last couple of weeks and will remain in that role with Robinson going on injured reserve due to a hamstring issue.

Defensive lineman Drake Jackson was elevated from the practice squad to round out the day’s moves.

sports.title: Patriots activate Mack Hollins from IR
sports.summary: The Patriots won't have A.J.
sports.body:
They have activated Mack Hollins from injured reserve. Hollins returned to practice this week after missing the last four games with a calf injury.

Hollins had 15 catches for 209 yards in four appearances before his injury. He had 46 catches for 550 yards and two touchdowns in his first season with the Patriots.

Brown will miss his second straight game with a knee injury and Doubs remains on injured reserve. Pop Douglas, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams join Hollins as the available receivers on the 53-man roster for New England.

sports.title: Vikings WR Jauan Jennings declined 49ers interest because "I love where I'm at"
sports.summary: Wide receiver Jauan Jennings has not played a major role in the Vikings offense through the first eight weeks of the season, but he wasn't interested in switching teams when the possibility presented itself last month.
sports.body:
The 49ers and Vikings discussed a trade that would send Jennings back to the team he played for during his first five NFL seasons and talks progressed to the point that Jennings spoke to his former coach Kyle Shanahan about a return. Jennings expressed a desire to stay with the Vikings and gave a succinct reason for his decision when asked about it on Saturday,

“I just thought it was best for both teams,” Jennings said, via Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com. “No distractions. I love where I’m at.”

Jennings only has six catches on 10 targets this season, but he expressed no issues with his spot in the Vikings’ offense.

“I’m not the coach, so I don’t call the plays,” Jennings said. “I’m a player, so I just play the game. I feel like anybody who watches football, who watches sports in general, kind of understands what comes with it.”

Jennings won’t be improving on his production Monday night as the Vikings ruled him out with a calf injury. That could open the door for Odell Beckham Jr. to make his Vikings debut.

sports.title: Bills list Dion Dawkins as questionable to play on Monday night
sports.summary: Dion Dawkins didn't practice at all this week, but the Bills aren't counting him out for Monday night's game against the Vikings.
sports.body:
Dawkins has been listed as questionable to play. A rib injury is the reason that Dawkins is at risk of missing a game for the first time this season.

The Bills ruled out wide receiver Joshua Palmer after he missed practice all week with a hamstring injury.

Offensive lineman Alec Anderson (ankle), defensive lineman Greg Gaines (calf), defensive back Jordan Hancock (hamstring), and wide receiver Tyrell Shavers (knee) are listed as questionable. Hancock and Shavers would need to be activated from injured reserve and the physically unable to perform list in order to play on Monday.

sports.title: Cowboys place OLB Malachi Lawrence on IR, activate OLB Marist Liufau from IR
sports.summary: The Cowboys placed outside linebacker Malachi Lawrence on injured reserve, the team announced Saturday.
sports.body:
Lawrence injured his ankle in Sunday’s loss to the Cardinals, and coach Brian Schottenheimer had announced the rookie would miss multiple weeks.

The first-round pick has 13 tackles, a sack and three quarterback hits, while playing 41 percent of the defensive snaps.

In a corresponding move, the Cowboys activated outside linebacker Marist Liufau from injured reserve. Liufau broke his forearm in the preseason finale. He returned to practice Oct. 22.

Cowboys defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard, who is in his 21-day return-to-practice window, will remain on injured reserve. He has a calf injury but had full practices all week.

The Cowboys also announced they elevated wide receiver Jordan Hudson and tight end James Mitchell from the practice squad.

Tight ends Jake Ferguson and Luke Schoonmaker are questionable to play, and at wide receiver, KaVontae Turpin is out and George Pickens is questionable.

sports.title: Philip Rivers completes high-school season, confirms interview with NC State
sports.summary: It's looking more and more like former NFL and NC State quarterback Philip Rivers will be the next coach of the Wolfpack.
sports.body:
Brian Murphy of WRAL has posted video of Rivers’s comments from last night, after the high-school team he coaches exited the playoffs in Alabama.

Rivers confirmed that he recently interviewed for the job, which became open two weeks ago when Dan Doeren was fired in his 14th season at NC State. Rivers immediately became a candidate. By last weekend, Rivers reportedly emerged as the focus .

Since then, the Wolfpack also interviewed former NFL and NC State quarterback Russell Wilson.

“We’ll see what the future holds,” Rivers said, adding that he plans to “take it one day at a time.”

If he goes, it will end his tenure at St. Michael Catholic High School in Fairhope, Alabama. He became the head coach in 2021.

“We didn’t have a stadium a few years ago,” Rivers said, turning emotional. “If it were to be the last time out here, shoot, a lot was accomplished.”

If it was the last time for Rivers at St. Michael, it means there will be a first time for him never year at NC State.

sports.summary: Wide receiver Jauan Jennings passed on a possible trade back to the 49ers in order to remain with the Vikings, but he won't be in Minnesota's lineup against the Bills on Monday night.
sports.body:
The Vikings ruled Jennings out due to a calf injury that kept him out of practice the last two days. Jennings has six catches for 54 yards this season, but his limited role in the offense didn’t cause him to reach for the exit door last month.

With Jennings out, the Vikings could elevate Odell Beckham Jr. from the practice squad to make his first appearance for the team. The Vikings have until Monday afternoon to elevate him for the game.

Quarterback Kyler Murray was ruled out with a hamstring injury earlier this week. Carson Wentz will make his second start of the season on Monday night.

Running back Demond Claiborne (knee) will also miss the game. Safeties Theo Jackson (quad) and Jay Ward (knee) are listed as questionable.

sports.title: Commanders activate DT Johnny Newton from injured reserve
sports.summary: The Commanders are activating defensive tackle Johnny Newton from injured reserve, Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports.
sports.body:
Newton has spent the season on IR after tearing a pectoral muscle in the preseason.

sports.title: Joe Burrow can become third quarterback with four or more TD passes in four straight games
sports.summary: Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow had seven touchdown passes in his team's first four games of the season.
sports.body:
With four against the Dolphins, four against the Ravens, and five against the Titans, Burrow has the chance to become only the third quarterback in NFL history to throw four or more touchdown passes in four straight games.

Via NBC Sports research, the two others were Colts quarterback Peyton Manning in 2004 and Dolphins quarterback Dan Marino in 1984. Both won the league MVP award in their seasons of four straight four-or-more touchdown games.

Burrow’s odds of winning the MVP for 2026 are currently at +475, behind only Josh Allen and Brock Purdy.

Burrow currently leads the league with 20 touchdown passes. And the Bengals, after starting 2-2, are now 5-2.

They face the 3-5 Falcons on Sunday morning in Madrid at 9:30 a.m. ET on Sunday.

sports.title: Saints release RB Kendre Miller
sports.summary: The Saints, on the last day before their first game since Week 7, have made a change.
sports.body:
Via Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.football, the Saints have waived running back Kendre Miller.

Miller arrived as a third-round pick (71st overall) out of TCU in 2023. He has 184 career carries for 656 yards, a per-carry average of 3.56 yards. He also has 29 career catches for 217 yards.

The Saints presumably tried to trade Miller but found no takers. He’ll now go to waivers. If he clears waivers, he’ll become a free agent.

Travis Etienne, who arrived in free agency, remains on injured reserve with a hamstring injury. The Saints currently have Alvin Kamara, C.J. Donaldson, and Audric Estimé on the depth chart. Estimé arrived recently on waivers from the Browns.

The 2-5 Saints host the 5-3 Browns on Sunday. The Saints hope to avoid their first 0-4 start at home since 1980 (not including the “home” game in Paris). That year, the Saints went 0-8 at home.

sports.title: Rams activate Myles Garrett, put Jaylen Watson on IR

Running back Ronnie Rivers will also be available after being activated from injured reserve. Tight end Terrance Ferguson was expected back as well, but was scratched on Friday with a hamstring injury.

Cornerback Jaylen Watson will not play as he suffered a season-ending shoulder injury. He was placed on injured reserve Saturday and the Rams also elevated long snapper Jake McQuaide and cornerback Damarion Williams from the practice squad.

sports.title: Report: Colts are in trade talks regarding QB Daniel Jones
sports.summary: The list of "multiple teams" currently includes the Ravens (who pivoted elsewhere) and the Vikings.
sports.body:
According to ESPNFL, the Colts have engaged in trade talks this week regarding Daniel Jones, speaking to “multiple teams.”

The precise language of the report identifies only one team as actually talking to the Colts. From the article, the Ravens “were one team to check in on Jones.” The Ravens ultimately struck a deal with the Cardinals for quarterback Jacoby Brissett, whose plunge from No. 1 to No. 3 on the depth chart made it clear to the rest of the league that he was available.

The only other team mentioned by name is the Vikings, and the report points only to "[s]peculation” involving Minnesota. (We’ve been “speculating” about it since the immediate aftermath of Sunday’s loss by the Vikings in Detroit.)

Past ESPNFL reporting on a potential trade for running back Jonathan Taylor ultimately listed five teams as talking to the Colts (Giants, Seahawks, Broncos, Packers, Vikings). The fact that other teams weren’t mentioned as to Jones suggests that, frankly, there may not be other teams.

Really, which current contender would want him? The Vikings are the only potential playoff team that checks the box as possibly needing a starter right now. And only the Vikings and Giants are contenders with which Jones has direct experience. (The Giants wouldn’t want a Jones reunion, and Jones surely wouldn’t want it, either.)

That could change this weekend, obviously. One injury to a starter could alter the dynamics, spurring another contender to pick up the phone and make a push for Jones. The most memorable example of that came 15 years ago, when a broken collarbone to Raiders quarterback Jason Campbell prompted a quick deal for Bengals quarterback Carson Palmer, who had decided he didn’t want to play for the team that had drafted him — and who had yet to report.

Three years ago, Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins popped an Achilles tendon two days before the deadline, forcing the Vikings to scramble at the deadline to do a deal with the Cardinals for quarterback Josh Dobbs.

Absent a multi-week injury to a starting quarterback on a contender that doesn’t believe its backup can hold down the fort, the Vikings may be the only team that wants Jones at the deadline.

sports.title: Report: Broncos are seeking a tight end trade, Cardinals rebuffed request for Trey McBride
sports.summary: Denver would like to acquire a veteran tight end before Tuesday's trade deadline, but that tight end will apparently not be Arizona's Trey McBride.
sports.body:
The Broncos have checked in with multiple teams about potential tight ends they could trade for, and that included the Cardinals, who told the Broncos they’re not interested in trading McBride , according to ESPN.

McBride is 26 years old and under contract through 2029, so it’s no surprise that the Cardinals see him as part of their future, although there’s never any harm in one GM calling another to see if a player is available. If the Broncos thought there was any chance they could get him, it was smart to ask.

The Broncos’ top tight end, Evan Engram, has just 13 catches for 136 yards this season. Sean Payton would love to get more production out of the tight end position than that. It won’t be a surprise if several more teams with potentially available veteran tight ends hear from the Broncos between now and Tuesday.

sports.body: This is not exactly a shock, but now we have a report from a national insider about what the Buffalo Bills are looking for at the NFL trade deadline. That insider is Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer. I recently tweeted the lack of reports this season represents a stark contrast to recent years, when the Bills were listed in essentially every trade-deadline insight article in the weeks leading up to the deadline. Now, there was one mention of the Bills’ intentions, from Breer, in late October. We wrote about here at Rumblings. It was one sentence and relatively vague compared to the rest of the mentions pertaining to other teams and trade chips. “The Bills are looking for another piece or two on defense.” This time around, in a response to a tweet that highlighted the lack of a Bills mention in his latest trade-deadline article, Breer wrote this: [Media: https://twitter.com/AlbertBreer/status/2119045872382050641?a=2_ae_CVVbMOxsdpgV5s&s=20] The positions are the unexpected part. However, the Bills have recently added Tre’Davious White and Kader Kohou to the practice squad at cornerback. They just got a quality effort from Te’Cory Couch in the slot. sports.title: Myles Garrett: Rams' opponents will have to pick their poison, me or Aaron Donald
sports.summary: Garrett and Donald will play together for the first time on Sunday against the Commanders.
sports.body:
Donald did not play in Week 1 because he was still ramping up for the season after returning from his two-year retirement, and Garret hasn’t played since Week 1 because of knee surgery. Garrett said the two of them together, two multiple-time Defensive Player of the Year award winners side by side, will present a unique challenge for opposing offenses.

“I think offenses really have to pick their poison. Who’s going to be freed up this play? I think either of us are pretty good at winning one-on-one, so we’ll have some fun,” Garrett said. “Going into this season I never thought I’d have the chance, and as you all know he kept us in suspense for quite a while, so it was very exciting, and I’m looking forward to getting on the field and playing some real snaps with him.”

Garrett said his poor performance in Week 1 against the 49ers showed him he needed knee surgery, something he would have preferred to avoid.

“I was frustrated after the game. I knew that wasn’t me, and I was being hampered by something,” Garrett said. “I didn’t want to miss any time, but I had to be realistic about where I was physically, and I had to make the best choice for me and the team.”

But now Garrett is back, and he said he and Donald playing together can give the Rams an “elite defense” for the rest of the season.

sports.title: Rams listed Matthew Stafford with elbow injury because reporters asked about ice on it
sports.summary: On Monday, reporters asked Rams coach Sean McVay about quarterback Matthew Stafford having ice on his throwing arm after Sunday's win over the Chargers.
sports.body:
“Really, it’s because you guys asked me about it earlier in the week,” McVay told reporters on Friday regarding the decision to disclose an elbow injury for Stafford. “It’s more semantical than anything else. It’s normal, like what he told you guys, but because you guys asked me about him having ice on his elbow. . . . He’s been full, hasn’t missed any sort of reps so normal management stuff that he’s been doing over the last few years.”

It conjures memories of the Patriots’ one-time habit of listing former quarterback Tom Brady as “probable” with a “right shoulder” injury. That all started because he had ice on his shoulder in the locker room, reporters inquired, and the team decided to just put him on the injury report every week.

“I haven’t seen any of that,” McVay said. “I told you guys he’d be better equipped to talk about it. He’s been a full participant, been awesome. He’s spinning the ball. He’s been able to activate all parts of the field with great timing, rhythm, and accuracy so he’s been great.”

So either he has an actual elbow injury that the Rams had been concealing, or he doesn’t really have an elbow injury but they listed him as having one because reporters noticed ice on his arm and asked McVay about it. Neither explanation seems to reflect the true spirit of the injury report, which expects real injuries — and only real injuries — to be disclosed.

Either Stafford has an elbow injury that was previously hidden or he doesn’t have an elbow injury and the claim that he has one is a middle finger to the meddling reporters who were doing their jobs. Neither explanation is a preferred alternative to the unvarnished truth.

sports.title: In defending his willingness to spend, Jerry Jones may have admitted to tampering
sports.summary: On Friday, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones tried to reverse the perception/reality that he deliberately underspends on coaches.
sports.body:
“I have been trying to lure very successful coaches away from the teams they were on,” Jones said on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas.

Unless he was referring to college coaches (or high-school coaches), that’s tampering. Period. End of discussion.

It could be false — an effort to bolster the idea that, yes, he’s willing to spend. Still, the effort to put out the frugality fire he started on Tuesday by ridiculously claiming there’s no correlation between coaching pay and winning included a nonchalant concession that he has tried to pry NFL coaches away from their current teams, in blatant violation of the rules.

Will the NFL look into this one? Probably not. Because the league office surely realizes, as the rest of us do, that Jerry was simply saying whatever he had to say to lessen the impact of the accidental truth he told on Tuesday regarding a deliberate reluctance to do whatever he needs to do to make his team as good as it can be.

sports.title: Nick Sirianni admits that he misled reporters about quarterback situation
sports.summary: Instead of covering up one lie with another lie, Sirianni opted to tell the truth that he hadn't.
sports.body:
Because they all do. Particularly in so-called “must-lie” situations.

There’s an art to it. A way to conceal a lie with another lie. On Friday, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni opted not to lie about the fact that he lied on Monday when he told reporters that quarterback Tanner McKee would not be benched.

“ Tanner’s our guy ,” Sirianni said. “We’re not making any changes there.”

On Wednesday, the Eagles made a change there, elevating Joe Milton over McKee. The move was announced after Sirianni had his midweek media availability, which prevented him from being asked questions about the change in position from “Tanner’s our guy” to “Tanner’s not our guy.”

On Friday, Sirianni finally faced the music regarding his comments from Monday. In lieu of coming up with an explanation premised on the idea that what he said was true when he said it and circumstances changed, Sirianni surprisingly admitted that he wasn’t telling the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth to reporters and, in turn, the fans.

“I was going to hold onto that as long as I possibly could, every second, every minute,” Sirianni said. “Again, I’m not real shy with you guys. I’m going to tell you what I want to tell you guys. I respect the job that y’all have to do, but I’m going to tell you what I want to tell you guys because I’m always going to protect the team first and foremost.

“Every second that goes by in a situation like that, that you can hold onto information as long as you possibly can, is a little less time for the opponent to get ready for the game. I know there’s a lot of interest in everything that you all want to hear, the fans want to hear. My job is to win football games, do everything we can do to help win football games, protect the guys here on this football team, and handle everything that I can inside.”

In an industry where the truth is only told when it’s coincidental to strategic interests, it’s jarring that Sirianni told the truth that he was lying. It would have been easy to say, “We took a more careful look at the situation after Monday.” Or, even more simply, “We changed our mind. Shit happens.”

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings have been playing football against each other since 1971. But in more than five decades, they’ve met just 15 times. Minnesota holds a 9-6 advantage in the all-time series, although Buffalo has won four of the past six meetings. And, while there aren’t a whole lot of games to choose from, there are certainly a few worth remembering. There’s the afternoon Drew Bledsoe threw for more than 400 yards. The day a rookie Josh Allen introduced himself to the NFL by hurdling a linebacker. And, of course, there’s that game in 2022 that Bills fans would probably rather forget. So, before Allen heads back to Minnesota, we’re opening the Time Capsule to revisit five of the more memorable meetings between the Bills and Vikings, starting with a comeback in 1982. _____________________________________________________________________________ 1982 — A comeback worth remembering The Minnesota Vikings had a 19-0 lead over Buffalo on Sept. 16, 1982, and every reason to think they had the game under control. Joe Ferguson, however, had other plans. The Bills offense was a little late to the party, but it was about to make up for lost time. Ferguson threw for 330 yards and three touchdowns as Buffalo rallied for a 23-22 win. He got the Bills on the scoreboard with a 6-yard touchdown pass to Frank Lewis before halftime, then connected with Jerry Butler for a 4-yard score in the third quarter. Minnesota still held a 22-13 lead heading into the fourth, but a 21-yard field goal from Nick Mike-Mayer brought Buffalo within six. Ferguson and Butler connected again, this time from 11 yards out, and Mike-Mayer’s extra point gave the Bills the win. _____________________________________________________________________________ 2002 — An overtime shootout The Bills and Vikings combined for 78 points on Sept. 15, 2002, and somehow needed extra time and another six points to find a winner. Drew Bledsoe threw for a franchise-record 463 yards, but Buffalo needed a little last-second magic just to get the game into overtime. The Bills had taken a 36-32 lead on Bledsoe’s 3-yard touchdown pass to Peerless Price with 3:08 remaining, only for Minnesota to answer with a touchdown of its own and go ahead 39-36 with 26 seconds left. Bledsoe got Buffalo into position for a Mike Hollis 54-yard field goal as regulation expired. Then Bledsoe and Price delivered the finish.
